research_updates.title: Parcel and appeal records connect the SV1 development to RagingWire
research_updates.notes: Santa Clara's development record identifies the SV1 project at 1150 Walsh Avenue on APN 224-58-003, while NTT's current facility page uses 1160 Walsh Avenue. The county appeal report names RagingWire Data Centers Inc. on that APN. These records support the project-to-parcel link, but no address-renumbering instrument was located, so both official address forms remain disclosed. County appeal positions are not final tax bills or payments; employment and water figures remain pre-opening forecasts.

source.title: Santa Clara County Assessor - school districts meeting report dated April 30, 2025

source.notes: The Assessor's Appeals System tables identify RagingWire Data Centers Inc. and APN 224-58-003. Appeal 22.3790 reports a $159,579,996 County Verified value against a $79,738,800 applicant opinion; appeal 23.6405 reports $83,066,779 against $41,533,390. research_updates.title: Project boundary and construction audit
research_updates.notes: City planning, CEQA, permit and Legistar records were searched by APN 224-58-003, 1150/1160 Walsh Avenue, PLN2018-13128, CEQ2018-01049, BLD2019-53423, RagingWire and NTT for 2018-2026. The finaled principal permit supplies a $125,405,765 administrative job value and DPR contractor identity; it does not supply audited outlays, equipment split, worker hours, payroll, supplier payments or local retention. Later tenant fit-out permits are not treated as separate buildings or added to the principal value.

source.title: Building permit BLD2019-53423 — 1160 Walsh Avenue
source.notes: The official permit record is Finaled and describes a new four-story, base-isolated data center with mechanical, electrical, plumbing and site work. It reports job value of $125,405,765 and identifies DPR Construction Inc. as general contractor. Job value is an administrative permit amount, not audited expenditure, payment, local purchasing or total investment.

research_updates.title: Fiscal audit — regular parcel bills verified
research_updates.notes: The county tax portal was reviewed for APN 224-58-003 across fiscal years 2017-2018 through 2025-2026. Nine paid regular-bill principals are normalized; separately numbered supplemental bills are excluded to avoid overlapping assessment events. Santa Clara budget, agenda, state California Competes and financing-record searches found the developer-funded Oaks Junction agreement but no project-specific tax-credit award, bond subsidy or same-scope net fiscal result.

source.title: Santa Clara County property-tax details — APN 224-58-003
source.publisher: County of Santa Clara Department of Tax and Collections
source.notes: The official parcel page identifies 1160 Walsh Avenue, TRA 007-000, and annual regular bills for APN 224-58-003-00. The normalized series sums the two paid regular installments for each fiscal year and excludes separately numbered supplemental bills to avoid overlap. A parcel payment spans multiple taxing jurisdictions and does not establish NTT's economic incidence or a fiscal net.

research_updates.title: Operations audit — capacity is observed, employment remains forecast-only
research_updates.notes: NTT/RagingWire releases, current specification and careers pages were searched for SV1, Santa Clara, 1150/1160 Walsh, employees, jobs, payroll, wages, occupancy and revenue from 2018-2026. The 16 MW and 64,000-square-foot data-floor specifications are retained, while the existing up-to-40-job plan remains a pre-opening forecast. No realized site FTE, payroll, wage, rack occupancy, revenue or operating expense was found.

source.title: NTT Opens New Silicon Valley Data Center
source.notes: The operator announced SV1's opening on April 13, 2021 and described the four-story, earthquake-base-isolated facility and its 16 MW capacity. It supplies no realized site headcount, payroll, capital outlay, supplier spend or local community transfer.

research_updates.title: Resource audit — capacity and cooling design do not establish consumption
research_updates.notes: Operator, City water/sewer, Silicon Valley Power, CEQA and air-district sources were searched for electricity, demand, PUE, water, wastewater, emissions, generator run time and renewable energy. The operator reports critical-load capacity and closed-loop cooling, the CEQA record retains a pre-opening water projection, and the air permit supplies a generator count. No site meter, bill, observed peak, annual kWh, realized PUE, water, sewer, emissions or renewable share was found; no capacity-to-consumption model is added.

source.title: Silicon Valley SV1 Data Center
source.notes: The current operator page identifies 1160 Walsh Avenue and reports 16 MW of critical IT load and 64,000 square feet of data floor, plus closed-loop water cooling. These are capacity and area descriptors, not utilization, annual electricity, whole-building area, metered water or audited environmental performance.

research_updates.title: Community audit — activity found, quantified transfer not found
research_updates.notes: NTT/RagingWire community, ESG, press and local nonprofit searches used SV1, Santa Clara, donation, grant, volunteer, school, nonprofit and first responder for 2018-2026. An SV1 fire-department training drill is documented, but no project-specific cash amount, in-kind value, volunteer hours or recipient accounting was public. No community amount is inferred.

source.title: Community partners: Collaborating with first responders in Silicon Valley
source.notes: The operator describes hosting a Santa Clara Fire Department confined-space rescue drill at SV1. No cash transfer, in-kind valuation, participant hours or recipient accounting is disclosed, so no community-benefit amount is normalized.

research_updates.title: Investment and public-cost audit — infrastructure agreement is not a fiscal net
research_updates.notes: Land-sale, deed, financing, construction, substation and City budget records were searched by address, APN, RagingWire and NTT. Public sources disclose land purchase without a primary-record price and a $450,000 initial developer contribution toward actual Oaks Junction station costs, but not total project investment, completed contribution total, annual City operating cost or project-attributable police, fire, road, utility, administrative or financing cost. Only a tax-equal break-even threshold is modeled; no net benefit is asserted.

source.title: Substation Service Agreement for the RagingWire data center
source.notes: The signed agreement links the 1150 Walsh planning address to the RagingWire project, states anticipated maximum demand of 27 MVA, makes the developer responsible for actual station development costs and calls for an initial $450,000 developer contribution. The agreement does not disclose final project cost, completed payment total or same-scope annual public-service cost; no available direct metric safely represents the contribution.

research_updates.title: Supplier audit — participants are identifiable, payments are not
research_updates.notes: Permit, project-team, operator, carrier and contractor sources were searched for DPR Construction, BKF Engineers, Linesight, procurement, vendor, supplier, contract and payment. DPR is identified on the principal permit, and public project pages identify other professional participants, but no contract value, paid amount, supplier address at payment time or Santa Clara County retained share was found. The permit job value is not allocated among suppliers and no procurement multiplier is applied.

source.title: NTT SV1 Data Center
source.notes: The project page identifies RagingWire as client and describes civil engineering, surveying and construction-monitoring participation at SV1. It provides no contract value, payment, vendor geography at payment time or locally retained procurement amount.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00052227492: Two-pass public-evidence and corrective gap-closure audit for Flexential's Minneapolis-Chaska data center on parcel 30.0590020 at 3500 Lyman Boulevard. The review covered Carver County parcel, valuation-notice, tax-statement and payment records; City of Chaska permit, inspection, agenda, archive, budget, utility and annual-financial-report sources; Minnesota DEED, Revenue, statutory, environmental, workforce and utility-regulatory sources; federal environmental, workplace-safety and county-economic access points; current and archived operator, predecessor, career and ESG materials; contractor and supplier references; and education, workforce and recipient-reported community sources for 2013-2026. Twenty-three quantitative observations are preserved: a source-projected original investment lower bound; three later non-cumulative permit values; current floor area and critical-load UPS capacity; three annual parcel-tax payments; one current parcel-tax bill; five exact-parcel taxable-market-value stocks for payable 2023-2027; and eight historical Via West Inc. estimated-actual-value observations. The exact parcel statements crosswalk the 2023-2025 city-table values to parcel 30.0590020, but the duplicate value concepts are alternative assessor presentations and are not additive. Stream's facilities at 1706 and 1708 West Creek Lane, the IP Stream Minneapolis LLC development agreement and its municipal rebates are outside the selected 3500 Lyman Boulevard project boundary and are not duplicated in this fragment; the six base Stream rebate rows require reassignment or removal from this target by the orchestrator because project fragments are append-only. Permit values are administrative estimates and are not summed because scopes may overlap. Parcel taxes span all taxing jurisdictions and special assessments, not City-only receipts or net benefit. No synthesis fragment is added because candidate-by-candidate review found no defensible project inputs for construction labor, realized operating employment or payroll, supplier payments, metered energy or water, emissions, facility-specific incentive value, public-service costs, quantified community transfers, or a causal county employment, wage or GDP effect. prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Corrective public-evidence and candidate-modeling audit for Switch Las Vegas NAP7, the individual real-property parcel and original SUPERNAP building at 7135 South Decatur Boulevard. The review covered Clark County assessor and ownership history, Treasurer, Accela permits, rights-of-way, planning, air quality, budgets and financial reports; Nevada incentive, tax and utility-regulatory sources; operator, SEC, workforce, supplier and contractor materials; and recipient-reported community records for 2005-2026. Six direct observations remain after the corrective pass; no wider Core Campus capital expenditure, combined incentive audit, later facility, personal property, tenant equipment, vendor equipment, company-wide employment or parcel-transfer price is recast as NAP7 contribution. One modeled synthesis is retained under the last-resort modeling gate: the fiscal-year 2027 real-property bill defines an exactly same-account assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even threshold. It is not actual public cost, collected revenue, jurisdictional receipt or a net fiscal result. Candidate models for investment, construction, suppliers, operations, resources, community benefits, net fiscal effects and county employment, GDP and wages were rejected for missing facility inputs, incompatible scope or timing, overlap, non-identification or lack of decision relevance. NAP7 employment, payroll, local supplier payments, metered electricity and water, personal-property tax, realized abatement, jurisdictional receipts, actual project-attributable public costs and net fiscal impact remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00214321737: Corrective public-evidence and model-eligibility audit for Markley Group's Lowell data center at 2 Prince Avenue/1 Markley Way in Lowell, Middlesex County. The selected IM3 footprint is one building inside a three-building assessor parcel, so every sourced amount remains at campus or company/county scope and is unallocated to the selected building. State and City records preserve Phase I forecasts, cumulative investment, operating-headcount, TIF-savings and incentive evidence; assessor and tax records provide parcel-value stocks and one complete billed-tax year; permits provide discrete administrative values and contractors; MEPA and MassDEP records establish supporting electric work and permit-listed generators; and two recipient records verify separate community contributions. Forecasts, cumulative values, parcel stocks, billed taxes, permit values, permit-authorized equipment, white-space area and recipient funding remain distinct and non-additive. Source-family gap closure found no audited annual construction outlay, construction workforce or payroll, vendor payments or local-purchase share, facility payroll, metered annual electricity, project-attributable utility-upgrade cost, annual water or wastewater series, actual emissions, cash tax receipts, marginal public-service cost, fiscal net or causal county outcome. One last-resort synthesis survives: the exact FY2026 real-property-bill amount is reused only as a same-account public-service-cost break-even threshold, not as observed cost, collected revenue or a net fiscal result; all other contribution and GDP, employment and wage candidates are rejected individually in the project updates. prj_study_im3_building_00300974499: Corrective two-pass public-evidence audit of Apple Mesa at 3740 S Signal Butte Road. The selected IM3 object is one 1,338,261-square-foot mapped building footprint, while the assessor describes a 1,255,156-square-foot Computer Center improvement and the permit, tax, utility, FTZ and operator sources generally cover the whole converted facility or related supporting infrastructure. The account therefore retains campus, company-county and supporting-infrastructure facts as unallocated unless a source supplies a narrower crosswalk. Twenty-five direct observations are added: the assessor floor-area fact and twenty-four completed positive-valuation Apple-era permits omitted from the prior account. Permit valuations are administrative amounts and related permits or addenda are not summed. All direct tax, payment, investment, electricity, renewable-capacity and projection records already in the base account remain; no unsupported zero is introduced. Direct water use, wastewater volume, utility bills, facility payroll, worker residence, local supplier payments, realized IOC relief, project-attributable community payments, marginal public-service costs and causal county outcomes remain unresolved. prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective public-source audit for Microsoft's data-center property at 5150 Rogers Road and explicitly labeled wider Microsoft/Bexar County activity. Exact-site ordinance, permit, appraisal, and tax-account records remain separate from later campuses and regional disclosures; the three appraisal accounts and two taxable-account payments are not consolidated. Permit value is administrative, the original investment and employment figures are commitments, the 2013 employment threshold is a reported lower bound, and the water quantity is a projection rather than metered consumption. No Bexar-and-Medina total is allocated to this property. Annual construction expenditure, construction labor and residence, supplier payments, operating payroll and purchases, recipient-level tax distributions, marginal public-service cost, electricity consumption, water withdrawal or consumption, wastewater, actual emissions, and a recurring facility-level community series remain unobserved after the documented searches. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 evidence audit. modeled_syntheses.label: Annual local public-service-cost break-even threshold

period.label: Fiscal year 2025-2026 same-scope break-even threshold

scope.label: APN 224-58-003-00 regular property-tax account spanning the same local taxing jurisdictions

interval.interpretation: The threshold equals the verified recurring regular-bill parcel-tax contribution by definition; it is not an estimate of actual public-service cost.

provenance.detail: Verified FY2025-2026 regular parcel bill paid

modeled_syntheses.confidence_rationale: The threshold identity is exact for the verified regular-bill principal, while actual same-scope marginal public cost is unavailable.
modeled_syntheses.decision_relevance: States the public-cost level that would offset the latest verified recurring tax contribution without manufacturing a cost or net position.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Project-attributable fire, police, road, utility, administrative, infrastructure and financing costs for the same recipients and fiscal year

derivation.formula: annual marginal local public-service cost at break-even = verified regular parcel property-tax contribution
assumptions: The threshold is an identity, not an observed cost.
No supplemental bill, developer contribution, incentive, fee or indirect tax effect is added or netted.
No positive or negative fiscal margin is asserted.

limitations: The regular parcel bill spans several recipients whose marginal costs may differ.
Supplemental bills and the developer-funded substation are outside this recurring threshold.
modeled_syntheses.notes: No net fiscal result and no actual public-service-cost estimate; this is only a same-scope break-even threshold.

No supplier, construction, payroll, household-spending, tax-abatement, public-service-cost or fiscal-net model is retained because local inputs and same-scope evidence are insufficient. prj_study_im3_campus_00231769626: Residual synthesis after the Google The Dalles public-source audit. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparison gaps are retained because the direct record does not identify causal county outcomes. Each benchmark uses the available 2001-2005 pre-opening history, excludes all study counties from a 20-county inverse-distance-weighted donor pool, and carries a fit-sensitivity envelope. No model converts broad investment or permit values to jobs, onsite contractor counts to supplier output, utility-system loads to campus consumption, tax bills to payments, or unmatched incentive formulas and public costs to a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_campus_00675108684: Dedicated last-resort Boydton model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Retained syntheses are limited to exact arithmetic over cited compatible observations: a five-fiscal-year average of the operator-reported portfolio property-tax total, its explicitly conditional same-scope public-cost break-even identity, and annual sums of identified LVL/Herbert Fund 301 components. All remain unallocated, modeled rather than observed, and non-additive to their source totals. COF phase investment, operating headcount, construction, resources, suppliers, induced effects, causal comparisons and net fiscal impact were rejected because overlap, timing, scope or required project inputs remain unresolved.
legacy_first_entry_note: Equinix SV1 was operational in Santa Clara County more than twenty-one years before NTT SV1 opened. The NTT event is therefore rejected as the county's first operational entry. The broader 74-facility historical inventory has not been proven complete, so the county's true first entry remains unresolved and no treatment date is assigned.

project_description: NTT Silicon Valley SV1 is a single four-story colocation data center operated by NTT Global Data Centers at 1160 Walsh Avenue in Santa Clara, California, on APN 224-58-003, which planning records also identify as 1150 Walsh Avenue. RagingWire began the project in 2018, the City later finaled the principal base-isolated-building permit, and NTT announced the 16 MW facility's opening on April 13, 2021. This account covers that building and parcel, not later tenant fit-outs or NTT's wider Silicon Valley portfolio.
